title: Thyroid scintigraphy: five uptake patterns
summary: Panels compare normal thyroid, Graves disease, toxic multinodular goitre, toxic adenoma and thyroiditis.
text:
Panels compare normal thyroid, Graves disease, toxic multinodular goitre, toxic adenoma and thyroiditis.

The primary article maps A to normal thyroid, B to Graves disease, C to toxic multinodular goitre, D to toxic adenoma and E to thyroiditis. The figure combines scintigrams with an anatomical illustration.
reading: A: the reference pattern; B: diffuse uptake in Graves disease.
C: uneven hot and cold areas in multinodular goitre; D: a dominant hot nodule with suppressed surrounding uptake.
E: decreased or absent uptake in thyroiditis. These are source-described patterns, not independent diagnoses from the atlas.

questions.prompt: Which source panel represents Graves disease?
questions.explanation: The primary article maps A to normal thyroid, B to Graves disease, C to toxic multinodular goitre, D to toxic adenoma and E to thyroiditis.

references.title: Wikimedia Commons source image and file-level licence
Underlying source and caption

labels.note: Panel A is the source's normal thyroid pattern.
Panel B is the source's Graves disease pattern: diffuse, symmetrical uptake over both lobes. The atlas has one thyroid structure, so the marker sits on the right lobe; the uptake is not drawn.
Panel C is the source's toxic multinodular goitre pattern: uneven hot and cold areas across both lobes. The model shows the nodules across both lobes; the hot and cold uptake is not drawn.
Panel D is the source's toxic adenoma pattern: a dominant hot nodule with suppressed uptake in the rest of the gland. The model shows the nodule's position and size; the uptake is not drawn.
Panel E is the source's thyroiditis pattern: decreased or absent uptake. The atlas has one thyroid structure, so the marker sits on the left lobe; the diffuse uptake is not drawn.

atlas_note: Normal thyroid anatomy is orientation context only. The source panels show tracer uptake patterns; the atlas does not reproduce Graves disease, a toxic nodule or uptake intensity. Panel letters A-E follow the original figure.

summary: Uniform ventilation with regional diminished perfusion in a source-identified pulmonary embolism case.
text:

title: Balanced ischemia: SPECT, PET and angiography
summary: SPECT appears without perfusion abnormality while oxygen-15 water PET reveals widespread stress perfusion deficits; angiography confirms severe disease, described as balanced ischemia.
text:
SPECT appears without perfusion abnormality while oxygen-15 water PET reveals widespread stress perfusion deficits; angiography confirms severe disease, described as balanced ischemia.

Panel A shows tetrofosmin SPECT with no apparent perfusion abnormality in the source case. Panel B shows extensive H2-15O PET stress perfusion deficits that partly improve at rest. Panel C shows source-marked severe coronary stenoses. The comparison illustrates this case's balanced ischemia.
reading: Panel A shows tetrofosmin SPECT with no apparent perfusion abnormality in the source case. Panel B shows extensive H2-15O PET stress perfusion deficits that partly improve at rest. Panel C shows source-marked severe coronary stenoses. The comparison illustrates this case's balanced ischemia.

questions.prompt: Which study shows widespread stress perfusion deficits despite the apparently normal SPECT pattern?
questions.answer: The H2-15O cardiac PET study in panel B
questions.explanation: The source describes apparently normal tetrofosmin SPECT, extensive stress PET deficits that partly improve at rest, and severe coronary stenoses on angiography.
